title: Direct Linear Transformation for the Measurement of In-Situ Peripheral Nerve Strain During Stretching
protocol: Attach a stereo-imaging camera system capable of capturing up to 100 frames per second to a utility stand.
Place two horizontally aligned cameras separated by a baseline of 63 mm on the stand.
Obtain three clear acrylic plexiglass square sheets, each measuring 12 inches by 12 inches by 0.125 inches.
On each sheet, place a grid and draw at least ten points.
Distribute a minimum of thirty points across the 3D control volume in the x, y, and z coordinate planes.
Construct the 3D control volume by stacking the three sheets at varying heights to capture the maximum height required for recording.
Digitize all points on the 3D control volume using a digitizer with a foot pedal.
Establish the origin (0, 0, 0) on the 3D control cube.
Define the positive x- and y-directions.
Open a document to save the digitized (x, y, z) coordinates in millimeters of each point.
Save the (x, y, z) coordinates as a *.csv file.
Use the digitized (x, y, z) coordinates to calibrate the stereo-imaging camera system's left and right cameras.
Attach the stereo-imaging camera system to a utility stand.
Position the stereo-imaging camera system 6 cm above the 3D control volume.
Connect the stereo-imaging camera system to a laptop via a USB type-C cable.
Open the imaging software.
Image the 3D control volume.
Run custom MATLAB code to separate the output image into two images, left and right views.
Click Run to initialize the DLTcal5.m GUI.
Click initialize on the DLTcal5 controls window to select the *.csv file with digitized (x, y, z) coordinates.
Select the corresponding image of the 3D control volume from the first view of the stereo-imaging camera system.
Select points in the order they were digitized in Section 2 to obtain 2D pixel coordinates from the left camera view.
Set current point on the DLTcal5 Controls window and click on the corresponding current point on the loaded first camera view image.
After selecting all the points, click compute coefficients to generate the 11 DLT coefficients for the left camera view.
Add a camera on the DLTcal5 controls window.
Repeat steps 3.7.2-3.7.6 to generate the 11 DLT coefficients for the right camera view.
Click save data on the DLTcal5 controls window to select the folder where output files will be saved.
Attach the stereo-imaging camera system to a stand and connect it to a laptop via a USB type-C cable.
Place the 3D control volume 6 cm under the stereo-imaging camera system.
Using the imaging software, take an image of the 3D control volume.
Separate the combined output image into individual left and right images using a custom MATLAB code.
Run DLTcal5.m.
Click initialize on the controls window.
Select the *.csv file with the digitized (x, y, z) coordinates of the 3D control volume.
Select the calibration image of the left camera view.
Select the points on the image in the same order that they were digitized.
Click compute coefficients to generate the DLT coefficients for the left camera view.
Click Add camera to repeat the steps for the right camera view.
Select the calibration image of the right camera view.
Select the points on the image in the same order that they were digitized.
Click compute coefficients to generate the DLT coefficients for the right camera view.
Click Save Data to select the directory to save the DLT coefficients for the left and right camera views.
Enter the name for the output file and click OK.
Place anesthetized neonatal Yorkshire piglet (3-5 days old) in a supine position with upper limbs in abduction to expose the axillary region.
Make a midline incision through the skin and fascia overlying the trachea down to the upper third of the sternum.
Use blunt dissection to expose the brachial plexus nerves.
Squirt saline solution on the exposed brachial plexus nerve to keep them hydrated before, during, and after testing.
Cut the distal end of a brachial plexus PN and clamp it to the mechanical testing apparatus.
Attach the stereo-imaging camera system to the utility stand, placing it up to 6 cm above the PN to be stretched.
Connect the stereo-imaging camera system to a laptop via a USB type-C cable.

Use an ink-based skin marker to place markers on the insertion and clamp sites and an additional two to four markers along the length of the PN depending on the nerve length, for displacement tracking.
Place a calibration grid (i.e., laminated grid with 0.5 cm x 0.5 cm squares) and a 1 cm ruler flat underneath the PN for data analysis.
Record the initial length of the PN after clamping and just before stretching.
Stretch the PN at a displacement rate of 500 mm/min to failure or a predetermined stretch.
Attach the stereo-imaging camera system to a stand.
Connect the stereo-imaging camera system to a laptop via a USB type-C cable.
Place the stereo-imaging camera system up to 6 cm above the peripheral nerve.
Clamp the peripheral nerve to the mechanical setup at the distal end.
Mark the insertion and clamp sites on the peripheral nerve with an ink-based skin marker.
Place two to four additional markers along the length of the nerve.
Squirt saline on the peripheral nerve before, during, and after testing to keep it hydrated.
Run custom MATLAB code to separate the output video file into left and right camera video files.
Initialize the DLTdv7.m22 GUI by clicking Run.
Click new project on the DLTdv7 controls window to begin a new project.
Select the first video file from the left camera view and click open.
Select the second video file from the right camera view and click open.
Click yes to signify the video files were acquired from calibrated camera views via DLT.
Select the corresponding DLT coefficients *.csv file for the stereo-imaging camera system and click on open.
Ensure the frame number is set to 1 on the DLTdv7 controls window.
Set the current point to 1 on the DLTdv7 controls window.
Turn autotrack mode off on the DLTdv7 controls window.
Check update all videos, DLT visual feedback, and show 2D tracks on the DLTdv7 controls window.
Ensure that the tracking points are placed on the displacement markers of the PN.
Place point 1 on the insertion marker on Video 1, ensuring it is at the center of the insertion marker.
Move the placed point to the center of the insertion marker using keyboard shortcuts.
When a point is placed in Video 1, place point 1 on the insertion marker in Video 2 using the blue epipolar line as reference.
Move the placed point to the center of the insertion marker using keyboard shortcuts in Video 2.
Click add a point on the DLTdv7 controls window to add points on the other tissue markers to track their trajectories.
Refer to the current point on the DLTdv7 controls window to know which point is active.
Place point 2 on marker 1 in Video 1.
Use the blue epipolar line and keyboard shortcuts to place point 2 on marker 1 in Video 2.
Continue adding and placing points, first on Video 1 and then on Video 2, for all displacement markers along the length of the nerve between the insertion and clamp.
Ensure the frame number is on 1 and the current point is set to 1 on the DLTdv7 controls window.
Change autotrack mode to auto-advance from the dropdown menu.
Set autotrack predictor to extended Kalman from the dropdown menu.
Begin tracking of all placed points in Video 1 first.
Track marker trajectory by left-clicking on the center of the marker frame by frame until failure or end of the video.
Return to frame 1 and change the current point to point 2 from the dropdown menu after completing tracking for point 1 in Video 1.
Complete the tracking of all points in Video 1 by left-clicking frame by frame for each point until failure or end of the video.
Return frame number to 1 and set current point to 1 in the DLTdv7 controls window.
Begin tracking point 1's trajectory in Video 2 using the blue epipolar line from Video 1.
Follow the same steps (5.2.16-5.2.18) to track remaining points in Video 2.
Export points on the DLTdv7 controls window to export (x, y, z) coordinates of tracked points.
Select directory location for output files when prompted by a dialog box.
Set name of the output files as specified (i.e., nerve1_101-Jan-2001videoanalyzed_cal09.30_trial1_).
Choose flat format for saving in another dialog box.
Select no to calculate 95% confidence interval when prompted.
Confirm data export and saved to selected directory location.
Save project on the DLTdv7 controls window in the same directory as output files.
Set current point to 1.
Place point 1 on the insertion marker in Video 1.
Using the blue epipolar line in Video 2, place point 1 on the insertion marker.
Set current point to 2.
Place point 2 on marker 1 in Video 1.
Using the blue epipolar line in Video 2, place point 2 on marker 1.
Set current point to 3.
Place point 3 on marker 2 in Video 1.
Using the blue epipolar line in Video 2, place point 3 on marker 2.
Set current point to 4.
Place point 4 on marker 3 in Video 1.
Using the blue epipolar line in Video 2, place point 4 on marker 3.
Set current point to 5.
Place point 5 on marker 4 in Video 1.
Using the blue epipolar line in Video 2, place point 5 on marker 4.
Set current point to 6.
Place point 6 on the clamp marker in Video 1.
Using the blue epipolar line in Video 2, place point 6 on the clamp marker.
Set frame number to 1, current point to 1, autotrack mode to auto-advance, and autotrack predictor to extended Kalman.
Set current point to 1. On Video 1 file, begin tracking the insertion marker displacement by left-clicking frame-by-frame until the last frame.
Set frame number to 1 and current point to 2. On Video 1 file, begin tracking marker 1 displacement by left-clicking frame-by-frame until the last frame.
Set frame number to 1 and current point to 3. On Video 1 file, begin tracking marker 2 displacement by left-clicking frame-by-frame until the last frame.
Set frame number to 1 and current point to 4. On Video 1 file, begin tracking marker 3 displacement by left-clicking frame-by-frame until the last frame.
Set frame number to 1 and current point to 5. On Video 1 file, begin tracking marker 4 displacement by left-clicking frame-by-frame until the last frame.
Set frame number to 1 and current point to 6. On Video 1 file, begin tracking the clamp marker displacement by left-clicking frame-by-frame until the last frame.
Set frame number to 1.
Set current point to 1.
Enable autotrack mode to auto-advance.
Set autotrack predictor to extended Kalman.
Begin tracking the insertion marker (point 1) displacement by left-clicking frame-by-frame until the last frame.
Set frame number to 1.
Set current point to 2.
Using the blue epipolar line on Video 2 file, begin tracking marker 1 (point 2) displacement by left-clicking frame-by-frame until the last frame.
Set frame number to 1.
Set current point to 3.
Using the blue epipolar line on Video 2 file, begin tracking marker 2 (point 3) displacement by left-clicking frame-by-frame until the last frame.
Set frame number to 1.
Set current point to 4.
Using the blue epipolar line on Video 2 file, begin tracking marker 3 (point 4) displacement by left-clicking frame-by-frame until the last frame.
Set frame number to 1.
Set current point to 5.
Using the blue epipolar line on Video 2 file, begin tracking marker 4 (point 5) displacement by left-clicking frame-by-frame until the last frame.
Set frame number to 1.
Set current point to 6.
Using the blue epipolar line on Video 2 file, begin tracking the clamp marker (point 6) displacement by left-clicking frame-by-frame until the last frame.
Run a custom MATLAB code to import tracked 3D marker trajectories.
Enter the rupture time in seconds on the MATLAB command window.
Input the number of tracked points into the MATLAB command window.
Select the *_xyzpts.csv file containing 3D trajectories.
Choose the directory to save output length vs time plots.
Save change in length vs time plots to a specified directory.
Store strain vs time plots in the designated directory.
Generate an *.xls file with time, length, change in length, and strain data.
Calculate the distance between any two markers at any time point.
Determine the change in distance from the original/zero-time point.
Compute the percent strain using the calculated change in distance.
